paragraphs.text: The rain forecast for Wednesday falls outside the time covered by the new U.S. Drought Monitor map. The assessment released Wednesday still places all of Pontotoc County in severe drought or worse, with 22.75% in exceptional drought. The map describes conditions at 6 a.m. Central on Tuesday, Nov. 24.

The county’s figures match last week’s at every level. Extreme drought or worse covers 87.77% of the county. That includes the land in exceptional drought, the most intense category. The other 12.23% of the county is in severe drought.

The statewide picture did change. Extreme drought or worse spread from 53.56% of Mississippi on Nov. 17 to 66.91% on Nov. 24, an increase of 13.35 percentage points. The share in exceptional drought held at 27.75% statewide.

The National Weather Service’s Wednesday morning forecast for Pontotoc County put the day’s rain chance near 100% and the evening and overnight chance at 90%, with most nighttime rain expected in the evening. For Thanksgiving Day, forecasters expect mostly cloudy skies, highs in the mid-40s and west winds gusting up to 30 mph. The effect of this rain on the drought will have to wait for a later assessment.
